title: Tôi sạc điện thoại ở đây được không?
englishTitle: Can I charge my phone here?
pronunciation: toy sahk dyen thoai uh day dook khong
summary: Different ways to say "Can I charge my phone here?" in Vietnam, with the safe phrase, reusable pieces, and nearby next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use this when the place has power and you need permission or a spot to charge. This works in cafés, hotels, airports, and waiting areas. Start with the full phrase, then use the nearby rows when the conversation needs one more step.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: This pattern turns the phrase into a yes-or-no question. Keep the main need together so the question stays natural.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Tôi sạc điện thoại ở đây được không? is the safest default for "Can I charge my phone here?". Use this when the place has power and you need permission or a spot to charge. Say it slowly, then point, show your phone, or hold up the item if the other person needs more context.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this when the place has power and you need permission or a spot to charge. Use it in Wi-Fi, SIM, battery, charging, maps, and phone setup when one clear sentence will work better than a long explanation.

sections.title: Watch out
sections.body: Do not hand over your unlocked phone unless you trust the situation. Show the screen first.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Show the phone screen while you speak. A visible error message often explains the problem faster than more words.
